newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't sees Banespa deal on Wed.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't sees Banespa deal on Wed.

text.p: A Finance Ministry official said a deal allowing the federal government to take over Sao Paulo state bank Banespa is likely to be announced on Wednesday, a local television said.
The deal is part of a refinancing package for Sao Paulo's huge debt with the federal government.

Ministry Secretary Pedro Parente told TV Globo the deal would be similar to those signed with Minas Gerais and Rio Grande do Sul states, which last September sealed agreements with the federal government to restructure part of their debts.
Under the plan being negotiated, 20 percent of Sao Paulo's debt would be paid through asset sales. The remainder would be refinanced for 30 years paying interest per year of six percent.
The deal also requires that Sao Paulo transfers its controlling stake in its troubled state bank Banespa to the federal government.

Meanwhile, Gazeta Mercantil newspaper said Banespa showed a net profit of 786 million reais in the first nine months. The figures were included in a report sent by the bank's administrative council to Sao Paulo Finance Secretary Yoshiaki Nakano and Central Bank director Alkimar Moura.
Banespa has not published its balance sheets since December 1994, when the Central Bank took over management of the bank due to Sao Paulo's massive debt with it, Gazeta said.
The newspaper said Central Bank intervenors in Banespa may modify the balance sheet before it is published, which is likely to happen after the deal with the federal government is signed.
